items.stem: In September 1952 Richard Nixon went on national television to answer charges about a private fund, in what became known as the Checkers speech. What did that broadcast demonstrate about the new place of television and the mass media in American politics?
items.stemEs: En septiembre de 1952, Richard Nixon apareció en la televisión nacional para responder a acusaciones sobre un fondo privado, en lo que se conoció como el discurso de Checkers. ¿Qué demostró esa transmisión sobre el nuevo lugar de la televisión y los medios de comunicación masiva en la política estadounidense?

choices.text: A candidate could appeal straight to a national audience over the heads of his own party's leaders, and keep his place on the ticket
choices.textEs: Un candidato podía apelar directamente a un público nacional por encima de los dirigentes de su propio partido y conservar su lugar en la candidatura

choices.text: A televised debate between the two presidential nominees could decide an election, and this broadcast was the first debate of that kind to be carried
choices.textEs: Un debate televisado entre los dos candidatos presidenciales podía decidir una elección, y esta transmisión fue el primer debate de ese tipo en emitirse
choices.explanation: The first televised presidential debates came in September 1960, eight years later, between Nixon and John F. Kennedy. The Checkers speech was one man speaking alone, with no opponent present and no moderator.
choices.misconception: turns a single candidate's broadcast into the first televised presidential debate

choices.text: Paid advertising had arrived in campaigns, since this was the first political commercial ever bought on television
choices.textEs: La publicidad pagada había llegado a las campañas, ya que este fue el primer anuncio político comprado en televisión
choices.explanation: Paid political spots did arrive in the 1952 campaign — the short Eisenhower Answers America films were running that autumn. Nixon's broadcast was a half-hour of purchased time for a speech, which is a different thing from a commercial.
choices.misconception: merges a bought half-hour speech with the short political commercial of the same campaign

choices.text: Televised hearings could end a senator's career, as the Senate's censure of Joseph McCarthy showed shortly afterward
choices.textEs: Las audiencias televisadas podían acabar con la carrera de un senador, como mostró poco después la censura del Senado a Joseph McCarthy
choices.explanation: That really happened: the Army-McCarthy hearings were broadcast in 1954 and the Senate censured McCarthy that December. It is a second and later demonstration of television's political weight, not what this 1952 broadcast showed.
choices.misconception: answers with a different and later demonstration of television's political power

items.dokRationale: Recall of what one broadcast established. The student retrieves the significance attached to a named event; no comparison of television's effects on homes, politics and the economy is involved. A DOK 2 item on this standard requires that comparison.
items.explanation: Before television a candidate in trouble answered to his party's managers, who decided whether he stayed on the ticket. Nixon went past them to the audience and the telegrams came back in his favour, so the decision was effectively taken out of the managers' hands — the first clear case of a broadcast overruling a party organisation.
items.explanationEs: Antes de la televisión, un candidato en problemas respondía ante los dirigentes de su partido, que decidían si seguía en la candidatura. Nixon pasó por encima de ellos y se dirigió al público, y los telegramas volvieron a su favor, de modo que la decisión salió de hecho de las manos de los dirigentes: el primer caso claro de una transmisión que se impuso a una organización partidaria.

items.stem: In the economics of the American mass media into the late 1950s, a single advertiser usually sponsored and produced an entire television programme and the networks merely carried it. What ended that arrangement and moved control of programming to the networks themselves?
items.stemEs: En la economía de los medios de comunicación masiva estadounidenses hasta finales de los años cincuenta, un solo anunciante patrocinaba y producía por lo general un programa de televisión completo y las cadenas simplemente lo transmitían. ¿Qué puso fin a ese arreglo y trasladó el control de la programación a las propias cadenas?

choices.text: The Federal Communications Commission's freeze on new station licences, which was lifted in 1952
choices.textEs: La congelación de nuevas licencias de estación por la Comisión Federal de Comunicaciones, levantada en 1952
choices.explanation: The freeze is real: the commission stopped granting licences from 1948 to 1952 while it sorted out channel allocation. Lifting it multiplied the number of stations, which is a question about reach rather than about who decided what those stations showed.
choices.misconception: answers how television spread when asked who controlled its programmes

choices.text: Television advertising revenue overtook radio's in the middle 1950s, which gave the networks money of their own
choices.textEs: Los ingresos publicitarios de la televisión superaron a los de la radio a mediados de los años cincuenta, lo que dio a las cadenas dinero propio
choices.explanation: Television did pass radio in advertising revenue in those years, and a network with money is better placed to produce its own programmes. That is a condition that made the change possible, not the event that forced it — the money was already there while sponsors still owned the shows.
choices.misconception: offers the condition that made a change possible as the cause that produced it

choices.text: The arrival of colour broadcasting, which cost more than a single sponsor could carry on its own
choices.textEs: La llegada de la transmisión en color, que costaba más de lo que un solo patrocinador podía sostener
choices.explanation: Colour broadcasting did begin in the 1950s and spread slowly — most American homes did not own a colour set until the late 1960s. Sponsors were not driven out by its cost; the change in control came before colour was general.
choices.misconception: invents a cost pressure from a technology that spread after the change it is said to have caused

choices.text: The quiz-show scandals of 1958 and 1959, after which the networks took programming decisions in house
choices.textEs: Los escándalos de los concursos de 1958 y 1959, tras los cuales las cadenas asumieron internamente las decisiones de programación

items.dokRationale: The student must identify which of four real developments in the industry produced a specific structural change, which means reasoning about cause rather than recalling that sponsors once owned programmes.
items.explanation: The scandals made sponsor control a liability. When congressional hearings established that contestants on sponsored quiz programmes had been given answers, the networks could no longer say that what went out under their call letters was somebody else's responsibility — so they took the production decisions in house and sold advertisers minutes instead of programmes, which is the arrangement television has had ever since.
items.explanationEs: Los escándalos convirtieron el control del patrocinador en un riesgo. Cuando las audiencias del Congreso establecieron que a los concursantes de programas patrocinados se les habían dado las respuestas, las cadenas ya no podían decir que lo que salía al aire bajo sus siglas era responsabilidad de otro: asumieron las decisiones de producción internamente y vendieron minutos a los anunciantes en lugar de programas, que es el arreglo que la televisión ha tenido desde entonces.

items.stem: Television became the leading mass media of the American home inside a single decade: between 1950 and 1960 the share of homes with a set rose from under one in ten to roughly nine in ten. Which change in household life does that evidence most directly support?
items.stemEs: La televisión se convirtió en el principal medio de comunicación masiva del hogar estadounidense en una sola década: entre 1950 y 1960, la proporción de hogares con televisor pasó de menos de uno de cada diez a cerca de nueve de cada diez. ¿Qué cambio en la vida doméstica respalda más directamente esa evidencia?

choices.text: Families spent more of their evenings reading, because the broadcast day ended early and left the later hours free
choices.textEs: Las familias dedicaban más de sus noches a la lectura, porque la jornada de transmisión terminaba temprano y dejaba libres las horas más tardías
choices.explanation: Broadcast days did sign off before midnight in this period, so the reason is accurate. The movement ran the other way: time given to a new medium came out of radio listening, moviegoing and reading, and cinema admissions fell sharply across the same decade.
choices.misconception: reverses the direction of the change in how evening hours were spent

choices.text: Evening hours were increasingly arranged around a broadcast schedule set outside the household
choices.textEs: Las horas de la noche se organizaban cada vez más en torno a una programación fijada fuera del hogar

choices.text: Network radio's evening audience grew alongside television's, because the two media served different hours of the day
choices.textEs: El público nocturno de la radio en cadena creció junto con el de la televisión, porque los dos medios cubrían horas distintas del día
choices.explanation: Radio did survive, and it survived by changing — toward recorded music, local programming and listening in the car. Its evening network audience and its dramatic serials went to television, and the sponsors went with them.
choices.misconception: takes radio's survival in a new form as growth in the audience television took from it

choices.text: Households acquired their first refrigerators and washing machines in the same decade and for the same reason
choices.textEs: Los hogares adquirieron sus primeros refrigeradores y lavadoras en la misma década y por la misma razón
choices.explanation: Appliance ownership did rise again after wartime production stopped, and the postwar consumer market is a real and related story. Electric refrigerators and washers had been spreading through American homes since the 1920s and 1930s, so the 1950s were not households' first encounter with either.
choices.misconception: answers with a parallel consumer trend when asked what the ownership figure shows

items.dokRationale: The student must decide what a single ownership statistic can and cannot establish, and reject statements that go further than the figure allows or run against it. Recalling that television ownership grew in the 1950s is the DOK 1 version of this content.
items.explanation: Ownership on that scale in ten years means the set became the room's organising fact. A broadcast schedule is set outside the house and cannot be paused, so meals, bedtimes and conversation arranged themselves around hours chosen by a network — which is the change the figure supports, and the reason advertisers would pay for those hours.
items.explanationEs: Una propiedad de esa escala en diez años significa que el aparato se convirtió en el hecho organizador de la sala. Una programación se fija fuera de la casa y no se puede pausar, de modo que las comidas, las horas de dormir y la conversación se organizaron en torno a horas elegidas por una cadena: ese es el cambio que respalda la cifra, y la razón por la que los anunciantes pagarían por esas horas.
